context: seed: what a mature store for the reasoning-core HARD tier holds — no observation behind it; the fork is read off the family's prompt (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:106, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:115), its budgets (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:72, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:127) and the checkers (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:67, suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:82); the method is the lesson of the stream, not a convention of one instance, and it transfers from the moderate tier unchanged; the lax pool budgets the knowing call plus one, the strict pool exactly the knowing call (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:72, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:127), and the tool layer counts a call before it refuses it (suite/tools.py:140, suite/tools.py:142)
counterfactual: The overshoot is the third call: a pass under the budget of two (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:72, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:127) that treats the checker as the search makes a third shell call, refused with `call budget of 2 exceeded at call 3` (suite/tools.py:142, suite/tools.py:145) and counted before the refusal (suite/tools.py:140), so the row fails tool_budget_respected while the task itself was solvable in one. The other overshoot is a first call that proves nothing — `python3 -c 'import nltk'` — which under the strict budget (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:72) leaves no call for the verification the method rests on.
decision: Treat the shell budget as exactly what the prompt states: every call counts — one refused past the budget and one that exits nonzero count too — and the budget is met when the verification is the first call. Spend no call finding out whether python3, `re` or `nltk` exist (they do), printing or echoing the pattern or grammar, listing files, or splitting one verification across calls; derive the candidate in reasoning and make the verifying call the first one, with the whole check in that one command (a heredoc is one call). Make the command exit 0 whatever the verdict — print True or False, never let an exception escape — so the one call always returns a verdict. If the verdict is False: under a budget of 1 do not call again — re-derive from the structure and return the re-derived candidate; under a budget of 2 the second call verifies one re-derived candidate and there is no third. Never make a call you expect to be refused: it is counted all the same.

residue: whether the re-derived candidate under a budget of one was right is judgment; the floor checks the call count against the budget

options.name: A — the verifying call is the first call; no probing, no printing, no splitting; under a budget of one a False verdict is repaired by re-derivation, not by a second call
options.why: the tool layer increments the counter before checking the budget (suite/tools.py:140, suite/tools.py:142), so an over-budget call is both refused and counted; python3 with re and nltk is on the PATH (suite/tools.py:28), so nothing needs probing

options.name: B — spend a first call checking the environment, then verify
options.why: the environment is known; the check costs the strict pool its only call and the lax pool its repair
